newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rails to sack 7,000 after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rails to sack 7,000 after restructuring.

text.p: A restructuring project of Croatia's railway company Hrvatske Zeljeznice financed by the World Bank will result in 7,000 job cuts, the company's Managing Director Marijan Klaric said on Wednesday.

"(Implementation of) the project is a pre-condition for getting loans, and we are expecting a $25-28 million loan from the World Bank when the (restructuring) process is over," the state news agency HINA quoted Klaric as saying.
A Canadian firm Canac is in charge of drafting the project, for which the Japanese government contributed $700,000, following a donation contract Croatia has signed with the World Bank.
The World Bank has previously approved an $80 million loan for the reconstruction of Croatia's road and railway system.
Klaric added that Hrvatske Zeljeznice had posted a 122 million kuna loss in the first half of 1996, and made only 54 percent of the planned turnover in the same period.
"Restructuring is a painful but unavoidable process and all monolith railway systems (in Eastern Europe) have to go through it," he said.
He added the Croatian railway network was in a terrible state, due to a four-year war that rendered a large part of the network non-operational.
Many tracks have to be demined while wagons and engines badly need revamping, Klaric said.
